title: Normalization tensor decomposition for a local weakly etale map
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian universally catenary local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, and let $C'$ be the integral closure of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], finite as a $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring and let $f:C\to D$ be a local weakly etale homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Here a local ring has one maximal ideal, local means its inverse image is the source maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero with no zero divisors. Then $D$ is reduced (an element whose positive power is zero is zero). Write $Q(D)$ for the total ring of fractions, obtained by inverting every nonzerodivisor of $D$, and $D'$ for the integral closure of $D$ in $Q(D)$. There is a canonical $D$-algebra isomorphism $C'\otimes_C D\cong D'$. For every minimal prime $P$ of $D$ (a prime with no strictly smaller prime), put $E=\overline{D/P}^{\,\operatorname{Frac}(D/P)}$. There is a commutative ring $F$ and a $D$-algebra isomorphism $D'\cong E\times F$ whose projection to $E$ restricts on $D$ to $D\to D/P\hookrightarrow E$. Tensor products have their usual algebra multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5 proof, first two sentences, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9): normalization base change cited as [4, Lemma 3.9], followed by the component product decomposition. The weakly etale map to the factor is derived in the item, not included here.

proof.text: Put $S=C\setminus\{0\}$, $T=K\otimes_C D$ and $H=C'\otimes_C D$. Flatness of $D$ over $C$ preserves multiplication by each nonzero $s$, so $f(S)$ consists of nonzerodivisors. Localization base change makes $T=f(S)^{-1}D$; localization at nonzerodivisors gives an injection $D\to T$.

Base change gives a weakly etale map K → T = K ⊗_C D. The proved source API Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul' applied to Algebra.WeaklyEtale.flat_lmul' makes T absolutely flat directly. Its reducedness and the injection D → T give reducedness of D.

The source theorem Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.exists_eq_mul_self_mul gives a = a*a*b for every a in T. Localization preserves nonzerodivisors. If a is the image of a nonzerodivisor of D, cancellation in this equation gives a*b=1. Thus every nonzerodivisor of D is a unit in T. The localization enlargement theorem IsLocalization.of_le identifies T canonically with Q(D). This replaces the finite-etale-subalgebra and product-of-fields detour of the previous plan.

source.place: Proofs of lemma-absolutely-flat (092F), lemma-absolutely-flat-over-absolutely-flat (092I), and lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field (092Q); the regular-element cancellation uses the proved source theorem Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.exists_eq_mul_self_mul.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] to the identity finite extension $K/K$. It says precisely that $C'$ is an integrally closed domain and $K$ is its fraction field. Base change of $C\to D$ along $C\to C'$ gives a weakly etale map $C'\to H$ by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]. Locality or a domain hypothesis on $H$ is not needed here.

The ambient ring for the weak-etale integral-closedness theorem is $H\otimes_{C'}K$. Commuting its two tensor factors and applying Mathlib's cancelBaseChange gives the isomorphism to $T=K\otimes_C D$ sending $(c'\otimes d)\otimes k$ to $(c'k)\otimes d$. The inverse sends $k\otimes d$ to $(1\otimes d)\otimes k$. Tensor balancing proves the pure-tensor formula, and this formula makes the isomorphism commute with $D$.

source.place: Tensor universal property and balancing; compare Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule)

proof.text: Now [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-integral-closure], applied to the integrally closed domain $C'$ with fraction field $K$ and the weakly etale algebra $H$, says that $H$ is integrally closed in $H\otimes_{C'}K$. Step 5 identifies this with the inclusion $H\hookrightarrow T$, so $H$ is integrally closed in $T=Q(D)$.

Every element of $C'$ is integral over $C$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change], and the swap $d\otimes c'\leftrightarrow c'\otimes d$, show that $H$ is integral over $D$. Thus the injection $H\hookrightarrow Q(D)$ has image contained in $D'$. Conversely, if $x\in D'$, a monic polynomial over $D$ annihilating $x$ is also a monic polynomial over $H$, since the inclusion of $D$ in $Q(D)$ factors through $H$ via $d\mapsto1\otimes d$. Integral closedness from Step 6 forces $x\in H$. The two subrings are equal, proving the canonical $D$-algebra isomorphism $C'\otimes_C D\cong D'$. Its map on pure tensors is $c'\otimes d\mapsto c'd$ in $Q(D)$, with $c'$ mapped through $K\to T$.

Apply the proved reduced-Noetherian total-fraction theorem to $D$. It supplies a finite indexing of the minimal primes and compatible maps from $Q(D)$ to $D_{P_i}$ whose product is bijective. Its residue-map bijectivity identifies each localization with $\kappa(P_i)$. Mathlib makes $\kappa(P_i)$ a fraction ring of $D/P_i$, so the canonical localization equivalence identifies it with $\operatorname{Frac}(D/P_i)$. All equivalences commute with the maps from $D$.

source.place: Tags 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points) and 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); compare morphisms.tex Tag 035P, parts (1)-(2)

proof.text: Projection sends an element integral over $D$ to one integral over $D/P_i$. Conversely, the quotient map $D\to D/P_i$ is integral, so transitivity makes each integral coordinate integral over $D$. Choose monic annihilating polynomials over $D$ for the finitely many coordinates and multiply them: each coordinate has a zero factor. This gives a bijective $D$-algebra map from the integral closure in the product to the product of the closures. The empty product satisfies the same argument.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), part (3); explicit coordinatewise monic-polynomial argument

proof.text: For the given minimal prime $P$, choose its index $j$ in the finite list of Step 8 and set $F=\prod_{i\ne j}E_i$ with its induced $D$-algebra structure. The isomorphism of Step 9 followed by the coordinate permutation and grouping $\prod_iE_i\to E_j\times\prod_{i\ne j}E_i$ is a $D$-algebra isomorphism $D'\cong E\times F$. Its first projection sends $d\in D$ to its class modulo $P$ in $E$, since the coordinate maps in Step 8 are precisely the localization and quotient fraction maps. If there is only one minimal prime, the empty product defining $F$ is the zero ring and the same maps apply.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NB-0377c9b2d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 10 steps and the statements of all 18 cited nodes. No new nodes were created and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and not weakened. The statement is true; I checked it on a field, a DVR, a non-normal domain with f=id, the reducible ring k[x,y]_(x,y)/(xy) and the one-minimal-prime case (F=0). Step 1: flatness of D over C makes f(S) nonzerodivisors and IsLocalization.tensor gives T=f(S)^{-1}D, so D and H inject into T. Step 2: base change and lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field (matches Stacks 092Q, more-algebra.tex l.30504) make T reduced, hence D reduced. Step 3: K[u] is finite etale, hence a product of fields; a zero coordinate would give an idempotent killed by u, so u is a unit and T=Q(D); I checked well-definedness and inverses of both fraction maps. Steps 4-6: C' is a normal domain with fraction field K, and 092W (l.30728, Lean-closed node) applies to C'->H, with the explicit isomorphism H(x)_{C'}K=T. Step 7: integral base change plus Step 6 gives H=D'. Steps 8-10: Q(D) is the product of D_{P_i}, each D_{P_i}=Frac(D/P_i), and the product of lifted monic polynomials gives prod E_i; the regrouping handles the empty product. The steps marked elementary really are. No duplicate found by rg over dag/nodes: the normalization-dimension, Nagata-ascent, total-fractions and minimal-product nodes all differ. lean.note: The canonical D-algebra comparison is specified by its fraction-clearing equation on every pure tensor: s*c=a implies f(s)*e(c tensor d)=f(a)*d in Q(D), for s nonzero. This uniquely determines its map. The minimal-prime factor uses the quotient-induced D-algebra structure.
